Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Wisconsin, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Ask for your ballot by

Thursday, October 29Passed

A request made by mail must reach your clerk by 5 p.m. on the 5th day before the election: Thursday, October 29, 2026. In person, you can ask and vote at your clerk's office from Tuesday, October 20 through Sunday, November 1, 2026, during the hours your city, village or town sets. (the law)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Your ballot must be delivered by 8 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. A ballot that arrives later is not counted, even if it was mailed earlier. (the law)

The last day to ask for a ballot by mail has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. Early voting in person runs through Sunday, November 1, 2026. When and where to vote early.

Ask for a ballot online, on Wisconsin’s own site

At school away from home, in Wisconsin or in another state? What Wisconsin says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

No reason is needed. State law counts as an absent voter anyone who, for any reason, is unable or unwilling to go to their polling place. You must be registered to vote before you can ask for an absentee ballot (military voters are the exception). (the law)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Online. Ask on MyVote Wisconsin, the Elections Commission's site. Like any written request, it needs a copy of your photo ID (military and overseas voters are exempt). Open it (the law)
  • By mail. Send a written request to your city, village or town clerk by mail, email or fax, with a copy of your photo ID. (the law)
  • In person. Ask in person at your clerk's office (or the other site your town names) and show your photo ID; you can vote there on the spot. (the law)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail the envelope to the clerk who sent you the ballot, early enough to arrive by 8 p.m. on Election Day. From outside the United States you add your own postage unless federal law makes it free. (the law)
  • In person. Deliver it in person to the clerk who sent you the ballot (or the other site your town names) by 8 p.m. on Election Day. (the law)

What the envelope needs

You need a copy of your photo ID with your request (unless you are a military or overseas voter, or the law exempts you). One adult U.S. citizen must watch you mark and seal your ballot and sign the envelope. The witness's address must be on the envelope; a ballot with the witness's address missing is not counted. (the law)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Wisconsin’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Tuesday, October 20, 2026 to Sunday, November 1, 2026.

Voting absentee in person at your clerk's office runs from Tuesday, October 20 (14 days before the election) through Sunday, November 1, 2026. Each city, village and town sets its own hours and place. (the law)

Students

At school in Wisconsin, away from home

State law says that for a student who lives in different places for parts of the year, if one of them is the parents' home, home for voting is the parents' home unless the student chooses to make a home elsewhere, for example by registering there. You do not lose your home by going to another part of the state for a temporary purpose while meaning to come back. The clerk mails an absentee ballot to your home address unless you tell the clerk to send it somewhere else, so a student registered at home can have it sent to school. (the law)

At school in another state, with Wisconsin as home

State law says you do not lose your Wisconsin residence by going to another state for a temporary purpose while meaning to come back. A student who keeps Wisconsin as home can ask for an absentee ballot and have it mailed out of state. (the law)

Military and overseas

Military voters (and their spouses and dependents) do not need to register first; they can give their details when they ask for a ballot, choose to get it by mail, email or fax, and do not need to send a photo ID. For November 3, 2026, the federal guide says a military voter's request must be received by 5 p.m. on Election Day (state law, section 6.86, sets 5 p.m. on Friday, October 30 for a military voter's request sent by mail); a citizen living overseas must register (postmarked by October 14, 2026; that date has passed) and ask by 5 p.m. on Thursday, October 29. The voted ballot must be mailed back and received by 8 p.m. on Tuesday, November 3, 2026. (federal guide)

Wisconsin in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • The Elections Commission's main website refused our request, so this record rests on MyVote Wisconsin and the state's statutes. Whether your town uses drop boxes, and the deadline for requests made online, by email or by fax, were not confirmed from an official page; ask your municipal clerk.
  • The Federal Voting Assistance Program's state guide was read through the content feed its own page loads.
